	\Big( \Delta \bar{D}^{\Ising}(q_d)\Big)
	\eeq
for $\sigma\in\{\RomI,\RomII,\RomIII\}$; 
as well as
	\beq
	\Delta\tilde{Q}^{\Ising}(q_d)
	\equiv
	\Delta\tilde{Q}^{\Ising}(q_d,B^\Ising)
	\equiv 
	\frac{1}{|B^{\Ising}|}
	\sum_{i\in B^{\Ising}}
	\Big(\Delta X^{\trunc,\Ising}(q_d,i)\Big)^2\,.
	\eeq
Denote also $E^{\sigma,\tau}\equiv Q^{\sigma,\tau}-\tilde{Q}^{\sigma,\tau}$. We define likewise $\Delta\tilde{Q}^\frozen$ using increments of $X^\frozen$. Then, 
analogously to \eqref{e:barD.vs.plus},
for all $\sigma , \tau \in\{\RomI,\RomII,\RomIII\}$ we have for $B^\frozen \cap [M] = B \neq \emptyset$
	\beq
	\Delta\tilde{Q}^{\frozen,\sigma,\tau}(q_d,B^\frozen)
	=\frac{|B|}{|B^\frozen|}

A similar relation holds between $\Delta\tilde{Q}^{\sigma,\Ising}$ and $\Delta\tilde{Q}^{\frozen,\sigma,\Ising}$, and likewise between
$\Delta\tilde{Q}^{\frozen,\Ising}$
and $\Delta\tilde{Q}^{\Ising}$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["the per-sample relative L2 loss as used by the EMIT/OCO-2 stacking pools; independent errors across rows","the multiplicative-versus-additive question is empirical and is measured by ens_rmt_elast.py (P21 of the RMT program)"],"created_at":"2026-09-05T11:47:28.061008+00:00","domain":"ensemble learning / weighted regression","id":"claim_c109e1a78941f0a6a45f877d2453aa489942de8d28e336dd0f0d21122d68470e","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Fitting a stack (or any linear predictor) under the per-sample relative L2 loss, mean over rows of ||y_i - yhat_i||^2 / ||y_i||^2, is weighted least squares with case weights s_i = 1 / ||y_i||^2. By the two-regimes corollary those are Aitken's variance-stabilising weights exactly when the error scale is proportional to the target norm (multiplicative error, elasticity of log ||e_i|| on log ||y_i|| equal to one); then the relative-metric fit is the efficient one and its optimism is 2m/n relative to its own noise level, regardless of how concentrated 1/||y_i||^2 is. If the error carries an additive floor, the rows with the smallest targets - exactly the rows the relative weights concentrate on - have the largest floor relative to their target, the concentration re-enters, and Kish's n_eff of the relative weights measures how far the fit is from balanced. The discriminating measurement is the elasticity of the out-of-fold residual norm to the target norm and the nonnegative fit ||e_i||^2 = a + b ||y_i||^2 (the floor share a / (a + b median ||y||^2)) on the calibration rows; on a pool whose targets vary by orders of magnitude (the EMIT radiance outputs) the question is live, on one whose targets are homogeneous (the OCO-2 retrievals, n_eff within a few percent of n) the two metrics coincide and it is moot.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["finite simple graphs (loops make P identically 0; parallel edges do not change P)","k a nonnegative integer in the counting definition; the polynomial identity then holds for all k"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T17:31:12.479653+00:00","domain":"graph theory","id":"claim_c11359eb703fe597fd324079d34608d788354417c8b886cc4a0e84bab112bea7","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"For a finite graph G and a positive integer k let P(G, k) be the number of proper colourings of the vertices of G with k colours (adjacent vertices receive different colours). THEOREM (Birkhoff, Whitney): P(G, k) is a polynomial in k of degree |V|, the chromatic polynomial, determined by the deletion-contraction recurrence P(G, k) = P(G - e, k) - P(G / e, k) for any edge e (G - e deletes the edge, G / e contracts it, merging its endpoints and removing loops and parallel copies), with P(empty graph on n vertices, k) = k^n. Facts: P(K_n, k) = k (k - 1) ... (k - n + 1); P(tree on n vertices, k) = k (k - 1)^{n-1}; P(C_n, k) = (k - 1)^n + (-1)^n (k - 1); P is multiplicative over connected components; its coefficients alternate in sign, the leading coefficient is 1, the coefficient of k^{|V| - 1} is -|E|, and the constant term is 0 for a graph with a vertex; the chromatic number is the least positive integer that is not a root; k = 0, 1, ..., chi(G) - 1 are roots; the chromatic polynomial is a specialisation of the Tutte polynomial, P(G, k) = (-1)^{|V| - c(G)} k^{c(G)} T(G; 1 - k, 0). Computing P is #P-hard in general, and evaluating it at k = 3 is #P-complete; the four colour theorem says P(G, 4) > 0 for every planar G.","status":"unverified"}

We study the analogous question for the sub-Gamma class underlying Bernstein's inequality, with the Laplace law as the majorant. Here the moment generating function is controlled by a Bernstein-type bound over a finite range of frequencies, rather than by a purely quadratic bound. We derive a variational formula for the optimal multiple, show that it is strictly larger than the natural scale $σ\\vee α$, and prove that this value is sharp, being attained by an asymmetric two-point distribution. We then turn to the sub-exponential class, which has a quadratic bound as in the sub-Gaussian case, but only over a bounded range as in the sub-Gamma case. Interestingly, the sub-exponential class displays a different behavior: the optimal multiple is exactly $σ\\vee α$, but is attained only when $α\\leq σ$; when $α> σ$, the constant remains sharp, but equality cannot hold for any non-affine convex function. Both results rely on a sharp finite-range variant of the Kearns-Saul inequality, which is of independent interest. (abstract text taken from the arXiv listing metadata; the TeX carried no abstract environment)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["Little: f entire and nonconstant","Great: f holomorphic on a punctured disk about a with an isolated essential singularity at a"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:49:42.482747+00:00","domain":"complex analysis","id":"claim_c11eee83f3cff31aeab34ce71916569c41ce2b6c167fbad02599fabb55fea697","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Little Picard theorem: if f is entire and nonconstant, then the complement of its image, C minus f(C), contains at most one point; i.e. a nonconstant entire function omits at most one complex value. Great Picard theorem: if f is holomorphic on a punctured disk 0 < |z - a| < r and has an essential singularity at a, then for every ε in (0,r) the image of the punctured disk 0 < |z - a| < ε is all of C with at most one point removed, and every value so attained (again with at most one exception) is attained infinitely often. Both exceptional values are genuinely possible and the count is sharp: exp(z) is entire and omits exactly the value 0, and exp(1/z) has an essential singularity at 0 and omits exactly 0 near 0. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:24:30.016157+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c12bf9d3c3a8abb63308ee247eecf7accaa4b1b45fcd8237561c328d3a969ba9","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 5 of arXiv:2605.05864, 'Classification and Metrization of Classes of Smooth measures'] \begin{enumerate}
\item A smooth measure \(\mu\) is {\it a Kato class measure} if it satisfies \( \lim_{\alpha \to \infty}\|U_\alpha \mu\|_{\infty, q} =0.\) Denote by \(\mathcal{K}\) the set of all Kato class measures.
\item  A smooth measure \(\mu\) is {\it a Dynkin class measure} if it satisfies \(\|U_1 \mu\|_{\infty, q} < \infty \). Denote by \(\mathcal{D}\) the set of all Dynkin class measures.
\item A Kato class measure \(\mu\) is {\it a Green-tight measure} for \(R_1\) if, for any \(\varepsilon >0\), there exists a compact set \(K\) such that \(\|R_1(1_{K^c}\mu)\|_\infty \leq \varepsilon\). Denote by \(\mathcal{K}_\infty= \mathcal{K}_\infty(R_1)\) the set of all Green-tight measures.

\item A Radon measure \(\mu\) has {\it finite energy integrals} if there exists \(C>0\) such that, for any \(f \in \mathcal{F}\cap C_c\), \(\int |f|d\mu \leq C\sqrt{\mathcal{E}_1(f,f)}\). Denote by \(\mathcal{S}_0\) the set of all Radon measures of finite energy integrals.

\item When $(\form,\dom)$ is transient, a Radon measure \(\mu\) has {\it \(0\)-order finite energy integrals} if there exists \(C>0\) such that, for any \(f \in \mathcal{F}\cap C_c\), \(\int |f|d\mu \leq C\sqrt{\mathcal{E}(f,f)}\). Denote by \(\mathcal{S}_0^{(0)}\) the set of all Radon measures of finite \(0\)-order energy integrals.
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

For $c \\ge 1$ let $\\mathcal{W}_c = \\{w : \\mathbf{1}^T w = 1,\\ \\|w\\|_1 \\le c\\}$, let $\\hat w \\in \\arg\\min_{w \\in \\mathcal{W}_c} w^T \\hat\\Sigma w$ and $w^* \\in \\arg\\min_{w \\in \\mathcal{W}_c} w^T \\Sigma w$. Then (i) $|w^T(\\hat\\Sigma - \\Sigma)w| \\le \\varepsilon\\, c^2$ for every $w \\in \\mathcal{W}_c$, and (ii) $0 \\le \\hat w^T \\Sigma \\hat w - w^{*T}\\Sigma w^* \\le 2\\varepsilon c^2$. {"assumptions":["Omega is bounded and open in R^n with C^1 (or piecewise C^1) boundary, so the divergence theorem applies","u is in C^2 up to the closure of Omega","for the Pohozaev form: u = 0 on the boundary, f is continuous, F(t) = integral_0^t f and F(0) = 0","for the nonexistence corollary: n >= 3, Omega star-shaped about the origin, f(u) = |u|^(p-1)u with p >= (n+2)/(n-2), and strict star-shapedness plus Hopf or unique continuation in the critical case"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T19:13:10.396148+00:00","domain":"elliptic PDE, variational identities and nonexistence","id":"claim_c1db80201085a9bde5ef4703381e7acf672f7231bfba2a288812bae9f615e2b6","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let Omega be a bounded open subset of R^n with boundary of class C^1 and outward unit normal nu. RELLICH IDENTITY: for every u in C^2(closure of Omega) one has integral_Omega (x . grad u) Laplacian(u) dx = ((n-2)/2) integral_Omega |grad u|^2 dx - (1/2) integral_{boundary} (x . nu) |grad u|^2 dS + integral_{boundary} (x . grad u)(du/dnu) dS. POHOZAEV IDENTITY: if in addition u = 0 on the boundary of Omega and -Laplacian(u) = f(u) in Omega with f continuous and F(t) = integral_0^t f(s) ds, then, since on the boundary grad u = (du/dnu) nu, the two boundary terms collapse and one gets ((n-2)/2) integral_Omega |grad u|^2 dx + (1/2) integral_{boundary} (x . nu) |du/dnu|^2 dS = n integral_Omega F(u) dx. CONSEQUENCE (nonexistence): let n >= 3, let Omega be star-shaped with respect to the origin (x . nu >= 0 on the boundary) with C^1 boundary, and let f(u) = |u|^(p-1) u with p >= (n+2)/(n-2). Multiplying the equation by u gives integral |grad u|^2 = integral |u|^(p+1), while Pohozaev gives ((n-2)/2) integral |u|^(p+1) + (1/2) integral_{boundary}(x . nu)|du/dnu|^2 = (n/(p+1)) integral |u|^(p+1). Since p >= (n+2)/(n-2) is exactly n/(p+1) <= (n-2)/2, the boundary term is <= 0 while star-shapedness makes it >= 0; hence it vanishes and integral |u|^(p+1) = 0 for p > (n+2)/(n-2). In the critical case p = (n+2)/(n-2) the two bulk terms cancel identically and one concludes only that (x . nu)|du/dnu|^2 = 0 on the boundary; if Omega is strictly star-shaped (x . nu > 0) this forces du/dnu = 0 on the whole boundary and then u = 0 by the Hopf lemma or unique continuation. WHERE IT FAILS: star-shapedness is essential, not technical - on an annulus {a < |x| < b} in R^n there exist positive radial solutions of -Laplacian(u) = u^p vanishing on both boundary spheres for EVERY p > 1, including supercritical p (Kazdan-Warner). Regularity is also essential: the identity is proved for u in C^2 up to the boundary (it is valid for H^1_0 weak solutions only after elliptic regularity has upgraded them, which requires growth conditions on f), and the boundary must be regular enough for the divergence theorem. The origin matters: star-shapedness is with respect to the point used in the multiplier x . grad u.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:53:51.726188+00:00","domain":"dispersive partial differential equations","id":"claim_c1ffc6c7824bf7e532852028244a4f3f17e1d97b6a2fce726d3b11f59a0d7c16","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Load-bearing hypothesis: in ‖e^{itΔ}f‖_{L^q_t L^r_x(R×R^n)} ≤ C‖f‖_{L²} the exponents must satisfy 2/q + n/r = n/2 exactly, and q ≥ 2 (and r ≥ 2). None of these can be relaxed, so an argument that 'interpolates' to a pair off the scaling line, or that uses a short-time-looking pair with q < 2, is wrong. Scaling: for f_λ(x) = f(λx) one has (e^{itΔ}f_λ)(x) = (e^{iλ²tΔ}f)(λx), hence ‖e^{itΔ}f_λ‖_{L^q_t L^r_x} = λ^{−2/q − n/r}‖e^{itΔ}f‖_{L^q_t L^r_x} while ‖f_λ‖_{L²} = λ^{−n/2}‖f‖_{L²}. If 2/q + n/r ≠ n/2 the ratio of the two sides is λ^{n/2 − 2/q − n/r}, which is unbounded as λ → 0 or λ → ∞ for any fixed f ≠ 0. So an estimate off the scaling line fails for every nonzero f. Necessity of q ≥ 2 (the case r > 2; on the scaling line r = 2 forces q = ∞, so there is nothing to prove there): take φ ∈ S(R^n) and f_N = Σ_{k=1}^N e^{−i t_k Δ}φ with t_1 ≪ t_2 ≪ ... ≪ t_N separated enough that Σ_{j≠k}|t_k − t_j|^{−n(1/2−1/r)} is small for every k. Since |⟨e^{isΔ}φ, φ⟩| ≤ (4π|s|)^{−n/2}‖φ‖_{L¹}² → 0, the summands are almost orthogonal in L² and ‖f_N‖_{L²}² ≈ N‖φ‖²_{L²}; and for t within O(1) of t_k the dispersive estimate makes every term but the k-th small in L^r_x, so ‖e^{itΔ}f_N‖_{L^q_t L^r_x} ≳ N^{1/q}‖e^{itΔ}φ‖_{L^q_t([−1,1]) L^r_x}. The ratio is ≳ N^{1/q − 1/2}, unbounded when q < 2. Known excluded endpoints, where the pair is on the scaling line and q = 2 but the estimate is still false: (q,r) = (2,∞) for Schrödinger in n = 2 (Montgomery-Smith), and (q,r) = (2,∞) for the wave equation in n = 3 (Klainerman–Machedon). Also for the wave equation the Lebesgue-space estimate is stated with r < ∞; at r = ∞ one must pass to Besov spaces.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["K = M = 2","eta in [2499/5000, 2501/5000]","start (q, c, r) = (1, 0, 0)","computer-assisted certificate, single author, unreviewed"],"created_at":"2026-10-16T11:27:20.250762+00:00","domain":"probability theory; learning dynamics","id":"claim_c26a5e333b10b5dad1a54b30467c9df70b35732bc2f77702a79bf60d4b0a9dd7","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Setting: online SGD for a soft committee machine with K students w_1..w_K in R^N and M = K orthonormal teachers v_1..v_K, activation g(x) = erf(x/sqrt 2), output sum_i g(w_i . x), Gaussian inputs, no noise, step eta/N. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-12T16:00:40+00:00","domain":"probability","id":"claim_c26dbe1967eabd9968a58da43f41afdfaebe56d66241b6d5ae45dbc5bb37aa7a","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Localized regime of the bounded-density conjecture for quadratic forms (Proposition 4). Let X_1..X_n be independent with densities <=1 and Q(x)=x^T A x with A symmetric. (a) If some 2x2 PRINCIPAL submatrix B of A (two original coordinates i, j) is definite, then ||p_Q||_inf <= pi/sqrt(det B). Proof: condition on the other n-2 ORIGINAL coordinates (independent, so Fubini is genuine); given them Q is a quadratic-plus-linear form in (X_i, X_j); complete the square (B invertible), which shifts (X_i, X_j) and keeps their joint density <=1; for definite B each set {s <= y^T B y <= s+h} is an elliptic annulus of area at most pi h/sqrt(det B), so the conditional density is at most pi/sqrt(det B); average. (b) Hence if A has a 3x3 PRINCIPAL submatrix A_[S] all of whose eigenvalues have modulus >= c>0, and A_[S] is definite or diagonal, then ||p_Q||_inf <= pi/c: for definite A_[S], Cauchy interlacing puts both eigenvalues of every 2x2 principal block of A_[S] at modulus >= c with one sign, so det >= c^2; for diagonal A_[S], two of the three diagonal entries share a sign and form a definite diagonal block with det >= c^2. This contains the separable case. (c) For other well-conditioned blocks the bound K/c is not proved. A block may have no definite 2x2 principal block at all, e.g. [[0,1,1],[1,0,1],[1,1,0]] (eigenvalues 2, -1, -1), and the rank-3 coarea bound ||p_S||_inf <= K||rho||_inf^{2/3} is false for general bounded densities on R^3: a density rho <= B placed on a thin shell around {S = s} gives p_S of order B s^{1/2}/sqrt(l1 l2 l3) for a definite form, unbounded in s. So the localized regime is settled for forms with a definite 2x2 principal block of determinant >= c^2, in particular when a well-conditioned 3x3 principal block is definite or diagonal; the other localized forms stay open, together with the DELOCALIZED forms (every 3x3 principal block near-singular), which is the CLT regime.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:16:49.564752+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c27395fdd622af983c5bbb8bf266923ee0bca3378e79f11affe6bc9e95d19078","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 18 (A sufficient condition for proxy-faithfulness) of arXiv:2608.25188, 'Transforms for LLM Quantization:\\ The Great Inversion and Format Co-Design'] Let transforms $A,B$ act on the same operand under a common grouping and produce group-RMS profiles with $\sum_g\sigma_g^2=S_A\ge S_B$ and per-group crest factors $M_g=\mathrm{CF}_g\,\sigma_g$ all lying in a band
$\mathrm{CF}_g\in[\underline c,\bar c]$ (necessarily $1\le\underline c\le\bar c\le\sqrt G$
for a group of size $G$). If that band is tight relative to the proxy gap,
$\bar c^2/\underline c^2 < S_A/S_B$, then the $L^2$ proxy $\sum_g\sigma_g^2$ and the
AbsMax step-size surrogate $\sum_g M_g^2$ rank $A$ and $B$ the \emph{same} way. When

{"assumptions":["mu and nu are measures on a common measurable space (X, Sigma); nu may be signed or complex","the epsilon-delta characterisation requires nu finite"],"created_at":"2026-09-13T01:59:23.251367+00:00","domain":"measure theory","id":"claim_c2889b5313a76c0af8fa3f49c365322c4a2e27291177d6ab0a182d09f34f8d7d","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let $\\mu$ and $\\nu$ be measures on the same measurable space $(X, \\Sigma)$, with $\\nu$ possibly signed or complex. $\\nu$ is absolutely continuous with respect to $\\mu$, written $\\nu \\ll \\mu$, if $\\nu(A) = 0$ for every $A \\in \\Sigma$ with $\\mu(A) = 0$ (for signed $\\nu$, equivalently $|\\nu|(A) = 0$, where $|\\nu|$ is the total variation). If $\\nu$ is FINITE (or finite signed/complex), this is equivalent to the $\\varepsilon$-$\\delta$ condition: for every $\\varepsilon > 0$ there is $\\delta > 0$ with $|\\nu(A)| < \\varepsilon$ whenever $\\mu(A) < \\delta$; for infinite $\\nu$ the $\\varepsilon$-$\\delta$ condition is strictly stronger (e.g. $\\nu(A) = \\int_A |x|^{-1}dx$ on $(0,1)$ has $\\nu \\ll$ Lebesgue but fails $\\varepsilon$-$\\delta$). Any measure of the form $\\nu(A) = \\int_A f\\,d\\mu$ with $f \\geq 0$ measurable (or $f \\in L^1(\\mu)$ for signed $\\nu$) satisfies $\\nu \\ll \\mu$; the Radon-Nikodym theorem is the converse under $\\sigma$-finiteness. $\\mu$ and $\\nu$ are mutually singular, $\\mu \\perp \\nu$, if there is $A \\in \\Sigma$ with $\\mu(A) = 0$ and $\\nu(X\\setminus A) = 0$. Lebesgue decomposition: for $\\sigma$-finite $\\mu, \\nu$ there is a unique splitting $\\nu = \\nu_{ac} + \\nu_s$ with $\\nu_{ac} \\ll \\mu$ and $\\nu_s \\perp \\mu$. Related but different: a FUNCTION $F: [a,b]\\to\\mathbb{R}$ is absolutely continuous iff its Lebesgue-Stieltjes measure is absolutely continuous w.r.t. Lebesgue measure iff $F(x) = F(a) + \\int_a^x F'$ with $F' \\in L^1$; the Cantor function is continuous, increasing, but not absolutely continuous (its measure is singular). Sharp edge: $\\nu \\ll \\mu$ is not symmetric, and $\\nu \\ll \\mu$ with $\\mu \\ll \\nu$ (equivalence) does not make the density bounded or bounded below.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:33:12.356302+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c28ac3ae4d8e7ea64f8166fb4e0c699b29ccee4086b9570d919c226f9391a1e9","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Dfn 232 (truncated Lipschitz algorithm) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Consider an $L$-Lipschitz algorithm $\cA_N$ with input $(\bG, \bg^\aux)$. Denote its output $\bx\equiv\cA_N(\bG,\bg^\aux)$. For $a\in [M]$, define the random variable
	\[\fm_a\equiv
		\fm_a(\bG,\bg^\aux;\cA_N)
		\equiv
		\frac{(\bg^a,\bx)}{N^{1/2}}\,,
	\]
where we recall that $\bg^a$ is the $a$-th row of $\bG$.
	For $K > 0$, define
	\[
		S_K(\cA_N) = \bigg\{
			a \in [M] : 
			\Big|\E\fm_a(\bG,\bg^\aux;\cA_N)\Big|
			\ge K
		\bigg\}\,.
	\]
Let $\hbG \in \R^{M\times N}$ be a matrix of i.i.d. gaussians independent of $(\bG, \bg^\aux)$.
	Then define the \textbf{truncated algorithm} $\cA_{N[K]}$ as the function
	\[\cA_{N[K]}\Big(\bG, 
	\bg^{\aux+}
	\equiv(\bg^\aux, \hbG)\Big)
	\equiv
	\cA_N\Big(\tbG(\bG,\hbG;S_K(\cA_N)), \bg^\aux\Big)\,,
	\]
where $\tbG$ is the row-splicing operation from Definition~\ref{d:row.splice}. In words, if $|\E\fm_a| \ge K$, then $\cA_{N[K]}$ ignores the $a$-th row $\bg^a$ of $\bG$ and replaces this input with the independent gaussian vector $\hat\bg$. 	Clearly $\cA_{N[K]}$ is also an $L$-Lipschitz function, with output
	\[\tilde{\bx} \equiv 
		\cA_{N[K]}(\bG, (\bg^\aux, \hbG)) \stackrel{\textit{d}}{=}
		\bx
		= \cA_N(\bG, \bg^\aux)\,.
	\]
It follows that $\cA_{N[K]}$ is also an $L$-Lipschitz algorithm in the sense of Definition~\ref{d:Lip}.","status":"unverified"}

r\in L^1_{\rm loc}.

Then the almost-everywhere function in~\eqref{eq:weak-normal-flux} admits a right-continuous representative of locally bounded variation. For every pair of continuity levels $s_0<s_1$, one has
\bel{eq:weak-Gauss-Green}

{"assumptions":["the transversal obstruction is for the cyclic square (Cayley table of Z_n) with n even; it does not transfer to arbitrary Latin squares of even order","Tarry's result is specific to order 6; orthogonal mates exist for every order other than 2 and 6","a transversal is a set of n cells, one per row, column and symbol"],"created_at":"2026-09-02T07:51:33.048970+00:00","domain":"combinatorial designs (hand-authored statement with hypotheses, 2026-09-02)","id":"claim_c2a935feb9d5a1be9d3032095348234a9a1e5cc7691477012e8f97b64cdb76ec","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Tarry (1900) showed by exhaustion that no Latin square of order 6 has an orthogonal mate, so Euler's thirty-six officers problem has no solution; a pair of orthogonal Latin squares exists for every order n except n = 2 and n = 6 (Bose, Shrikhande, Parker 1960, refuting Euler's conjecture for all n congruent to 2 mod 4 beyond 6). A Latin square has an orthogonal mate if and only if it can be decomposed into n disjoint transversals. For the cyclic Latin square of order n (the Cayley table of the integers mod n): when n is odd the diagonals give n disjoint transversals, so it has an orthogonal mate; when n is even it has no transversal at all, because a transversal would be a complete mapping of Z_n and the sum of all elements of Z_n, n/2, is not zero (a parity obstruction), so in particular it has no orthogonal mate. The even-order cyclic result is a statement about the cyclic square only; other Latin squares of the same even order (n = 4, 8, 10, ...) can have transversals and mates.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:35:04.099460+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c2d28f0baa6f776c6936e59f735c71b2aa18a4aca176624ec07279506b86c5a9","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:maximal-selected-slice of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] Put $j_i=\sqrt2a_i$, $\widehat A_i=\operatorname{ad}_{j_i}$, and let

\[
 \mathcal F_{B,i}(Y)=\frac1{\sqrt N}\left(

and, for
\[

\[

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T10:15:36.154577+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c2eb21a5cc39c0c3fffe3fb5b1b7a2350df0572a37ca7f08d6204162f254e734","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 10 (Product-shell bookkeeping) of arXiv:2609.01570, 'A Proof of Fraenkel's Conjecture'] For distinct \(a,b\in A\), write
\[
 d_{ab}=\normQ{ab^{-1}},\qquad P_{ab}=bd_{ab}.
\]
Then
\[
 P_{ab}\in\{a,Q-a,Q+a,2Q-a,2Q+a,\ldots\},
 \qquad \frac1{d_{ab}}=\frac b{P_{ab}}.
\]
For every \(a\in A\), every subset \(B\subseteq A\setminus\{a\}\),
and all real numbers \(L\ge0\) and \(T>0\), if
\[
 \sum_{b\in B}b\le L
 \qquad\text{and}\qquad
 P_{ab}\ge T\quad(b\in B),
\]
then
\[
 \sum_{b\in B}\frac1{d_{ab}}\le\frac LT.
\]
Also, \(P_{ab}=a\) implies \(b\mid a\).

In the special case \(s=1\), call \(b\) good when
\(b\mid Q-1\) or \(b\mid Q+1\).  If such a good \(b\) satisfies
\(P_{ab}\in\{Q-a,Q+a\}\), then \(b\mid a-1\) or \(b\mid a+1\).
If moreover \(a>1\) and \(b>a\), this forces \(b=a+1\).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:52:47.241752+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c3092bf5adfd353dc1b6027a3f20a6ae44e2f31050c739a2a2102928d191e63b","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 3 (weak pullback calculus) of arXiv:2609.01093, 'Ideal MHD below the classical well-posedness threshold'] Let $X$ be an orientation-preserving global bi-Lipschitz map as above.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] $E_i$ is skew-adjoint on $L^2(\mu)$. In particular
  \[
   \int_{\Real_y^n}(E_if)\phi d\mu=-\int_{\Real_y^n}f(E_i\phi)d\mu
  \]
  whenever $f,\phi,E_if,E_i\phi\in L^2(\mu)$.
\item[(ii)] Let $F=F^i\eframe_i$ be a vector field along $X$ whose Cartesian components belong to $L^1_{\rm loc}(\Real^n_y;\Rn)$. If
  $q,c^{ij}\in L^1_{\rm loc}(\mu)$, then
  \[
   \Div_{\gmetric}F=q,
   \qquad
   (\curl_{\gmetric}F)^{ij}=c^{ij}
  \]
  in the conjugated distributional sense if and only if
  \[
   \partial_a(J\Kmat_i^aF^i)=Jq,
   \qquad
   \partial_a\!\left(J\Kmat_i^aF^j-J\Kmat_j^aF^i\right)=Jc^{ij}
   \quad\text{in }\mathcal D'(\Real^n_y).
  \]
  Equivalently, for every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Real^n_y)$,
  \begin{equation}
   \int q\varphi d\mu=-\int F^i\Kmat_i^a\partial_a\varphi d\mu,\qquad
   \int c^{ij}\varphi d\mu=-\int\bigl(F^j\Kmat_i^a-F^i\Kmat_j^a\bigr)
          \partial_a\varphi d\mu.
  \end{equation}
  With the convention in \eqref{eq:metric-tensor-divergence}, the same
  calculation gives, whenever
  $H:=\Div_{\gmetric}T\in L^1_{\rm loc}(\mu)$,
  \begin{equation}
   JH^j
   =\partial_a(J\Kmat_i^aT^{ji})
   \quad\text{in }\mathcal D'(\Real_y^n)
  \end{equation}
  for every locally integrable tensor $T$.
\item[(iii)] If $\mathcal C_X^{-1}F\in W^{1,p}_{\rm loc}$ for some
  $1\le p\le\infty$, then 
  \begin{equation}
      \partial_aF^i=A_a^jE_jF^i,
  \end{equation}
  and the conjugated divergence and curl in
  (ii) agree almost everywhere with the pointwise formulas $\Kmat^a_i\partial_aF^i$ and
  $\Kmat^a_i\partial_aF^j-\Kmat^a_j\partial_aF^i$.
\item[(iv)] The conjugated derivatives commute on their common
distributional domain:
  \[
   E_iE_j=E_jE_i.
  \]
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:41:19.332925+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c34bf893bf5ec8cf799e4a64a9eea7a14e57e7781d1c9df9d7d0e002328a8935","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem {\cite[Theorem~1.1.4 and Remark~1.1.5 of arXiv:2609.04138, 'The conformally invariant metric on $\CLE_4$ I:\\ subsequential limits of the non-simple C'] {LevelLineGFFI}}]
Suppose that $h$ is a GFF on $\BH$ with piecewise constant boundary conditions that change only finitely many times. For all $u \in \BR$ and $x \in \partial \BH$, we let $\gamma_u^x$ be the level line of $h$ with height $u$ starting from $x$ and ending at $\infty$ (when it exists). Fix $x_2 \leq x_1$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $u_2 < u_1$, then $\gamma_{u_2}^{x_2}$ a.s.\ stays to the left of $\gamma_{u_1}^{x_1}$ (possibly touching it).
\item If $u_2 = u_1$, then $\gamma_{u_2}^{x_2}$ may intersect $\gamma_{u_1}^{x_1}$ and, upon intersecting, the two curves merge and never separate.
\item If $u_1 - u_2 \geq 2 \lambda$, then $\gamma_{u_1}^{x_1}$ and $\gamma_{u_2}^{x_2}$ do not intersect each other a.s.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["X is a Banach space","A is dissipative","the range condition Ran(λ_0 − A) = X (or dense) is the hypothesis at issue"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:53:42.772454+00:00","domain":"functional analysis, operator semigroups, boundary value problems","id":"claim_c354d651b0d3d4c7e46b9aa4b5480a1f39abee205e5d85399db455e11dffea4d","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Load-bearing hypotheses: A is densely defined, dissipative, AND Ran(λ_0 − A) = X (or at least dense) for some λ_0 > 0. What fails without the range condition: a dissipative operator can be closed and densely defined and still generate nothing. Counterexample: X = L²(0, 1), A f = f' with D(A) = {f ∈ H¹(0,1) : f(0) = f(1) = 0}. Then A is densely defined and closed, and Re⟨f', f⟩ = (|f(1)|² − |f(0)|²)/2 = 0, so A is dissipative (indeed both A and −A are). But solving λf − f' = g with f(0) = 0 gives f(x) = −∫_0^x e^{λ(x−s)}g(s) ds, and the second boundary condition f(1) = 0 forces the constraint ∫_0^1 e^{−λs} g(s) ds = 0: Ran(λ − A) is a closed subspace of codimension 1, not dense, for every λ > 0. Hence A is not a generator, although dropping one boundary condition (D = {f ∈ H¹ : f(1) = 0}) gives exactly the generator of the left shift semigroup. The range condition is what encodes 'the right number of boundary conditions'. What fails without density: X = C[0,1] with the sup norm, A f = f' on D(A) = {f ∈ C¹[0,1] : f(1) = 0}. Solving λ f − f' = g with f(1) = 0 gives f(x) = ∫_x^1 e^{λ(x−s)}g(s)ds, so ‖f‖ ≤ ‖g‖/λ: A is dissipative and Ran(λ − A) = X for every λ > 0. Yet the closure of D(A) is {f ∈ C[0,1] : f(1) = 0}, a proper closed subspace, so A generates no C_0-semigroup on C[0,1] (generators are densely defined); it generates one on the smaller space. Density is automatic only when X is reflexive, which C[0,1] is not. Related trap: for the norm inequality version, dissipativity means ‖(λ − A)x‖ ≥ λ‖x‖ for all λ > 0 - checking it for a single λ, or checking Re⟨Ax, x⟩ ≤ 0 only on a core without knowing the operator is closed or closable there, proves nothing about the closure being a generator unless the range condition is verified on that same core.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["(X, B, mu, T) is measure-preserving on a standard Borel (Lebesgue) probability space","mu is T-invariant; entropies are Kolmogorov-Sinai entropies with values in [0, +infinity]","the ergodic decomposition is taken over the sigma-algebra of T-invariant sets","convex combinations are of T-INVARIANT measures only","no finiteness of entropy and no continuity of the entropy map is assumed or asserted"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T19:09:43.732492+00:00","domain":"ergodic theory, entropy","id":"claim_c423ff08a284a7ccfc7dc1d8f089019abb153806f7c00355fd50d003464125fc","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let (X, B, mu, T) be a measure-preserving system on a STANDARD Borel (Lebesgue) probability space, and let I be the sub-sigma-algebra of T-invariant sets.

ERGODIC DECOMPOSITION. There is a measurable family x -> mu_x of T-invariant Borel probability measures on X such that (i) mu_x is a version of the conditional measure of mu given I, so mu(A) = integral of mu_x(A) d mu(x) for every A in B and integral of f d mu = integral over x of (integral of f d mu_x) d mu(x) for f in L^1(mu); (ii) mu_x is ERGODIC for mu-a.e. x; (iii) the family is essentially unique. Writing P for the law of the random measure x -> mu_x, one gets mu = integral of nu dP(nu) supported on the ergodic T-invariant measures -- the Choquet representation of mu in the simplex of invariant measures.

AFFINITY OF ENTROPY. Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy is affine in the measure, with values in [0, +infinity]:
  for every finite measurable partition Q,   h_mu(T, Q) = integral of h_{mu_x}(T, Q) d mu(x);
  and                                        h_mu(T)    = integral of h_{mu_x}(T) d mu(x).
In particular, for T-invariant mu and nu and t in [0,1],  h_{t mu + (1-t) nu}(T) = t h_mu(T) + (1-t) h_nu(T).

SHARP EDGES. (1) AFFINE IS NOT CONTINUOUS: nu -> h_nu(T) is affine on the simplex of invariant measures but is in general NOT weak-* continuous; for expansive homeomorphisms it is upper semicontinuous, and in general it can fail even that. Do not use affinity to pass to weak-* limits. (2) The decomposition genuinely needs a standard/Lebesgue space; on a pathological measure space conditional measures need not exist and the statement can fail. (3) The convex combination must be of INVARIANT measures -- entropy is undefined for a non-invariant measure, so there is no affinity statement along an arbitrary path in the space of measures. (4) The identity holds in [0, +infinity]; if h_mu(T) = +infinity the integral is +infinity, and no finiteness is assumed anywhere. (5) The affinity is a property of measure-theoretic entropy, not of topological entropy: the variational principle gives h_top(T) = sup over invariant nu of h_nu(T), which is a supremum over the simplex, so it is attained (if at all) at ergodic measures precisely BECAUSE h is affine -- but h_top itself is not an average.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-28T02:39:12.388242+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c48365866ce534c77114704d0db89b51cd9ee0418e1cdad2bbed722719835d1f","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem homo multilinear recursion of arXiv:2412.07936, 'Simple Norm Bounds for Polynomial Random Matrices via Decoupling'] [Homogeneous Multilinear Recursion]

Let ${\bf x} = \{x_i\}_{i = 1}^n$ be a sequences of i.i.d random variables with ${\mathbb E} x_i= 0$,  ${\mathbb E} x_i^2= 1$ and $|x_i| \leq L$ for all $1\leq i \leq n$. Let $\{{\bf A}_{{\bf i}}\}_{{\bf i} \in {\mathcal T}^d_n}$ be a multi-indexed sequence of deterministic matrices of the same dimension. Define a permutation symmetric, homogeneous multilinear polynomial random matrix of degree $d$ as
$$
{\bf F}({\bf x}) =  \sum_{{\bf i} \in {\mathcal T}^d_n} \left( {\bf A}_{{\bf i}} \cdot \prod_{j \in \{i_1,\dots, i_d \}} x_j\right).
$$
Let $a,b,c\in {\mathbb Z}_{\geq 0}$ and $d = a+b+c$. Then for $2 \leq t \leq \infty,$
$$
{\mathbb E} \norm{{\bf F}({\bf x}) - {\mathbb E} {\bf F}({\bf x})}_{4t}^{4t} ~\leq~ \sum_{\substack{a,b,c: \\ a+b+c=d}} (48dt)^{4dt} \cdot L^{4ct} \norm{{\bf F}_{a,b,c}}_{4t}^{4t}.
$$","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:33:12.350409+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c49ed582047c4cb6f5e89c53325b0de3d7f6b9478d7f83ec9740f9f1a7410e51","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem 179 (annealed second moment bounds for 
$\bar{D}^{\RomII}$ and 
$\bar{D}^{\frozen,\RomII}$) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Let $\bar{D}^{\RomII}$ and $\bar{D}^{\frozen,\RomII}$ 
be defined by \eqref{e:barD} and \eqref{e:barD.plus} (see also \eqref{e:drift.error.II}). We have 
the second moment bound 
	\[\frac{\E[\Delta\bar{D}^{\RomII}(q_d)^2]}
		{p(q_d)}
	\le \frac{L^{O(1)}\BUCKETS \delta}{N}\,,
	\]
for all $0\le d\le \dmax-1$. The same bound holds with $\bar{D}^{\frozen,\RomII}$ in place of $\bar{D}^{\RomII}$.
\begin{proof}
Recalling the notation from
\eqref{e:normalized.vectors.g} and \eqref{e:normalized.vectors.y},
we can rewrite \eqref{e:drift.error.II} as
	\[
	\frac{\Delta\bar{D}^{\RomII}(q_d)}
		{[\delta_d p(q_d)]^{1/2}}
	= 
	\frac1{|B|^{1/2}}
	\bigg(\frac{1}{N^{1/2}}\sum_{a\in B}
	\frac{\bar{\bg}^a(q_d)}{|B|^{1/2}},\by(q_{d+1})\bigg)
	\equiv
	\frac1{|B|^{1/2}}
	\bigg( \frac{\bar{\bg}^B(q_d)}{N^{1/2}},\by(q_{d+1}) \bigg)\,.
	\]
Note that $\bar{\bg}^B(q_d)$ is measurable with respect to $\cG(q_d)$. 
It follows by applying Lemma~\ref{l:y.subgaus} that 
	\[
	\frac{\E[\Delta\bar{D}^{\RomII}(q_d)^2]}{\delta_d p(q_d)}
	=\frac{1}{M}\E\bigg[\sum_{B\in\mathcal{B}(q_d)} 
	\bigg( \frac{\bar{\bg}^B(q_d)}{N^{1/2}},\by(q_{d+1}) \bigg)^2
		\bigg]
	\le \frac{L^{O(1)}}{M}
	\E\sum_{B\in\mathcal{B}(q_d)} 
	\frac{\|\bar{\bg}^B(q_d)\|^2}{N}\,.
	\]
We then note that if $\ind_B\in\R^M$ is the indicator of the coordinates in $B$, then
	\[
	\|\bar{\bg}^B(q_d)\|
	=\bigg\| \bar{\bG}(q_d) \frac{\ind_B}{|B|^{1/2}}\bigg\|
	\le \|\bar{\bG}(q_d)\|\,,
	\]
from which it follows that
	\[\frac{\E[\Delta\bar{D}^{\RomII}(q_d)^2]}{\delta_d p(q_d)}
	\le
	\frac{L^{O(1)}\BUCKETS 
		\E[\|\bar{\bG}(q_d)\|^2]}{MN}
	\le \frac{L^{O(1)}\BUCKETS}{N}\,,
	\]
where the last bound follows from Lemma~\ref{l:wishart}.
This proves the claim for $\bar{D}^{\RomII}$, and the claim for
$\bar{D}^{\frozen,\RomII}$ follows by using \eqref{e:barD.vs.plus}.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:13:18.507698+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c4a29a9821f86641b73c9a2bd61db74a52d87562589038f7e6c1d25cbde5925f","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 16 (From scalar wavelets to vector-valued wavelets) of arXiv:2608.30589, 'Vector-Valued Wavelet Bases as Hilbert $\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})$-Module Bases: A Construc'] Let $(\phi,\psi)$ be an orthonormal wavelet basis of $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ associated with an MRA.

Then the family
\[

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:50:30.562017+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c4a7efd4ffd532c6e9f1d326b2cbedbb130db89d3f3815a1d60f3704ee973b3b","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 13 of arXiv:2605.30560, 'Projected McKean--Vlasov Dynamics for Entropic Weak Optimal Transport'] A weak solution of \eqreftag{eq:cond-Fokker-planck-a} is a measurable map
\[
    \tilde \P:\R_+\times\Xc\longrightarrow \Pc(\R^d),
    \qquad
    (t,x)\longmapsto \tilde\P_{t,x},
\]
together with a Borel vector field
$
    \hat A:\R_+\times\R^d\longrightarrow\R^d,
$
such that the following conditions hold.

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*), ref=(\roman*)]
    \item 
    For \(\mu\)-a.e. \(x\in\Xc\), the map
    \(t\mapsto \tilde \P_{t,x}\) is weak continuous.

    \item 
    There exists \(p>1\) such that, for every \(T>0\),
    \[
    \int_0^T
    \int_\Xc
    \int_{\R^d}
    \left|
    \hat A(t,y)
    -
    a\bigl(t,x,y,\tilde\P_{t,x}\bigr)
    -
    \nabla_y V(y)

    =
    \E^{\tilde\P_{0,x}}[h]
    +
    \int_0^t
    \E^{\tilde\P_{s,x}}\!\left[
    \nabla h(Y)\cdot
    \left(
    \hat A(s,Y)
    -
    a\bigl(s,x,Y,\tilde\P_{s,x}\bigr)
    -
    \nabla_y V(Y)
    \right)
    +
    \Delta h(Y)
    \right]ds .
    \]

    \item

    $
    \P_t(dx,dy)
    :=
    \mu(dx)\,\tilde\P_{t,x}(dy),
$
    then, for a.e. \(t\ge0\),
    \[
    \hat A(t,y)
    =
    \E^{\P_t}\!\left[
        a\bigl(t,X,y,(\P_t)_X\bigr)
        \mid Y=y
    \right],
    \qquad

{"assumptions":["i.i.d. real summands","Lambda finite in a neighbourhood of 0, which makes Lambda^* a good rate function","the rate is exponential in n; polynomial prefactors are NOT captured"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:40.782174+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c4dfaffbd4e619148e1df048b6bc2f3b8bb7627b05d4a288d55a3707d2b749ea","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let X_1, X_2, ... be i.i.d. real random variables with cumulant generating function Lambda(lambda) = log E[ exp(lambda X_1) ] and Legendre transform Lambda^*(x) = sup_{lambda in R} ( lambda x - Lambda(lambda) ). Assume Lambda(lambda) < infinity for every lambda in a neighbourhood of 0. Then the empirical means S_n/n satisfy the LARGE DEVIATION PRINCIPLE with speed n and good convex rate function Lambda^*: for every closed set C, limsup_n (1/n) log P( S_n/n in C ) <= - inf_{x in C} Lambda^*(x), and for every open set G, liminf_n (1/n) log P( S_n/n in G ) >= - inf_{x in G} Lambda^*(x). In particular, for x > E[X_1], (1/n) log P( S_n/n >= x ) -> - Lambda^*(x), so the Chernoff upper bound is exact at the level of the exponential rate although it can be off by polynomial factors: the sharper Bahadur-Rao asymptotic supplies a factor of order n^{-1/2}. The exponential moment hypothesis is what makes Lambda^* a GOOD rate function, meaning its sublevel sets are compact; on the real line the large deviation principle itself continues to hold without it, but the rate function may fail to be good and the statement must then be handled with care. Heavy-tailed laws with no exponential moments have Lambda^* identically 0 above the mean, and their large deviations are governed by a single big jump rather than by a rate function of this shape. [Cramer (1938); see Dembo and Zeitouni, Large Deviations Techniques and Applications, 2nd ed., Theorem 2.2.3]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["i.i.d. (or stationary ergodic with care) elliptic environment on Z^d","The statement concerns the UNION of the two directional events","Directional 0-1 law is open for d >= 3"],"created_at":"2026-09-07T08:44:20.990370+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c4f0b35296bb24abc03e25c08c3620d73cbcb1dad336577101e148e2359e4818","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). Kalikow's zero-one law (1981; Zerner-Merkl 2001 for the sharp form): for random walk in an i.i.d. elliptic random environment on Z^d and a direction l, let A_l = {X_n . l -> +infinity}. Then P_0(A_l union A_{-l}) is 0 or 1. It does NOT say that P_0(A_l) itself is 0 or 1: the directional zero-one law P_0(A_l) in {0,1} is a theorem in d = 1 (Solomon) and d = 2 (Zerner-Merkl, using planarity: two walks in the same environment must intersect), and is an OPEN PROBLEM for d >= 3 (Drewitz-Ramirez Open Question 3.2; Kalikow's law is often misquoted as the directional one). Kalikow's proof: the event A_l union A_{-l} is invariant under a coupling of walks started at different points that follow the same environment after they meet in a slab, and its probability is a function of the environment's tail sigma-field, hence 0 or 1 by Kolmogorov. Consequences: under transience in some direction the regeneration structure of Sznitman-Zerner applies to the union event; Zerner's law of large numbers then gives X_n/n -> v or -c v. Typical failure: Treating Kalikow's zero-one law as if it determines transience, mistaking the statement that the probability is 0 or 1 for a claim that it equals 1; the theorem only rules out intermediate probabilities and leaves open, often genuinely unresolved, which side of the dichotomy holds for a specific environment law, which is precisely the content of the still largely open general ballisticity conjecture for random walk in random environment in dimension d>=2. Canonical reference: Kalikow, 1981, Annals of Probability; Zeitouni, 2004, Ecole d'Ete de Probabilites de Saint-Flour, Springer Lecture Notes in Mathematics.","status":"unverified"}

The family {exp(nz) : n ≥ 1} on the unit disk omits the value 0 everywhere, but it is not normal, not even in the extended sense: on the left half of the disk exp(nz) → 0 while on the right half |exp(nz)| → ∞, and a locally uniform limit on the connected set D would have to be holomorphic throughout or identically ∞. Montel's fundamental normality test needs two distinct omitted values, and that is sharp. (2) When two values are omitted, the conclusion is normality in the extended sense: the constant functions f_n = n omit 0 and 1 and converge to ∞, so a proof that assumes the limit is a finite holomorphic function must first exclude the ∞ branch (typically by a bound at one point or by the maximum principle). (3) Pointwise bounds are not local bounds. Montel's first theorem needs a bound uniform on each compact set; pointwise boundedness of the family is genuinely weaker (Runge's theorem produces sequences of polynomials converging pointwise on C to a discontinuous function, so such a sequence is pointwise bounded and not normal). (4) Normality is not convergence: it only yields subsequences, and the limit may leave the class one is working in — the injective maps z/n converge to a constant, and the limit of a normal family of functions in some prescribed family need not satisfy the same constraint unless Hurwitz-type arguments are added.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:35:04.100246+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c56ef7012a68ca3817605163ac67b912f6316ba2c63f6c2d28ac862d6d79eacb","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:heterogeneous-packet of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] Fix a circuit state $\tau$, including a maximizing smoothing, all

\[
 \mathfrak k_{\tau,v}(D)
 :=\max_{M\in\mathscr R_{\tau,v}}\|M(D)\|_{\rm op}.

\[

where the norm on the right is the invariant four-index

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-12T12:13:53+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c574fba2347e734a070686822f78efb69bc3f308b61775e623e7cd7013108c3f","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"For a real parameter delta >= 0 the SQUARED BESSEL PROCESS of dimension delta started at y >= 0, written BESQ^delta, is the unique strong solution of dY_t = 2 sqrt( |Y_t| ) dW_t + delta dt with Y_0 = y; the solution is nonnegative, and pathwise uniqueness holds despite the non-Lipschitz diffusion coefficient by the Yamada-Watanabe criterion, which requires only Holder continuity of exponent 1/2. The BESSEL PROCESS of dimension delta, BES^delta, is X_t = sqrt(Y_t); for X > 0 it solves dX_t = dW_t + ((delta - 1)/(2 X_t)) dt. When delta = d is a positive INTEGER, BES^d started at |x| has the law of the radial part |B_t| of a d-dimensional Brownian motion started at x - a fact that makes the family the natural interpolation of radial Brownian motion to non-integer dimension. ADDITIVITY: BESQ^delta started at y and an independent BESQ^{delta'} started at y' add to a BESQ^{delta + delta'} started at y + y'; this holds for the SQUARED process and is false for the Bessel process itself. The index nu = delta/2 - 1 is the other common parameterisation and is the one that appears in the modified Bessel functions of the transition density; delta and nu must not be confused. For 0 <= delta < 2 the point 0 is reached from y > 0, and the BESQ^delta equation itself fixes what happens there: 0 is absorbing for delta = 0 and instantaneously reflecting for 0 < delta < 2, so the squared process needs no extra boundary convention (the equation for X = sqrt(Y) holds only while X_t > 0). For delta >= 2 the point 0 is never reached from y > 0. [standard; e.g. Revuz and Yor, Continuous Martingales and Brownian Motion, 3rd ed., Chapter XI]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:48:30.919238+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c58d7bd3c00ae14afbf9fb38c6a5e7c51170ee1dda6fc27ba01135c99252a6aa","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Prop 10 (Derivations and $p$-Powers) of arXiv:2609.00974, 'On Algebraic Integrability\\ of Vector Fields \\ with Rational Function Coefficients\\ tha'] Let $K$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$. Let $x\in K$. Let $D,E$ be derivations on $K$.

    \begin{enumerate}
        \item The $p$-times composition 
        $D^{\circ p}=D^p$
        is a derivation on $K$.
        \item Derivations kill $p$-powers: 
        $$D(x^p)=0.$$
        In particular, all derivations are derivations over $k$.
        \item (Jacobson's formula) There exists a universal Lie polynomial $s$ such that 
        $$\left(D+E\right)^p=D^p+E^p+s(D,E).$$
        \item (Hochschild's formula) We have 
        $$\left(xD\right)^p=x^pD^p+\left(xD\right)^{\circ (p-1)}(x)D.$$
        \item We have
        \[
        [D,xE]=D(x)E+x[D,E].
        \]
    \end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:17:10.026141+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c5b407679b1fe1959a73a0566bb925060e9ec554806f1451d75afae06ecacbd7","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 23 of arXiv:2608.17374, '\textbf{On the Pseudo-Mixing of Kac's Walk}'] Let $(\mathcal{L}_t)_{t=0}^{T}$ be a nonnegative process adapted to a filtration $(\mathscr F_t)_{t=0}^{T}$. Let $\mathcal G\subseteq \mathscr F_0$ be an initial sigma-field, and let $B$ be a nonnegative $\mathcal G$-measurable random variable such that $\mathcal{L}_0\leq B$. Fix $\kappa\in(0,1]$, and let $G_0,\ldots,G_{T-1}$ be events with $G_t\in\mathscr F_t$.

Assume that, for every $t=0,\ldots,T-1$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item (\textbf{Deterministic non-expansion}) $\mathcal{L}_{t+1}\leq \mathcal{L}_t$ almost surely.
\item (\textbf{Good-step contraction}) On $G_t$,
\[
\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{L}_{t+1}\mid \mathscr F_t]\leq (1-\kappa)\mathcal{L}_t.
\]
\item (\textbf{Conditional bad-event control}) For deterministic numbers $\delta_t\geq0$,
\[
\mathbb{P}(G_t^c\mid \mathcal G)\leq \delta_t.
\]
\end{enumerate}
Then
\be
\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{L}_T\mid\mathcal G]
\leq \left((1-\kappa)^T+\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\delta_t\right)B.
\ee","status":"unverified"}

Here and below, the second-order part is read in divergence form:

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:35:04.100535+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c5d743010e1f522afded0398e85b7da7eab393f1c09777e938919c67e0db18c6","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:chronological-renewal of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] Fix a reflected two-replica monomer--dimer word with
$r\le L\log n$ nonconstant slots and one rooted spatial ribbon map
$\Gamma$.  Keep every same-time packet as one fused physical supernode,
every packet token once, the coupled pure-Weyl root, and the complete
finite-gap and weak chronological sums.  Remove the
scalar Jacobi child $-\gamma N^{-1}I$ before forming residual components.
Fix a reduced temporal record $\omega$ which records
all data listed in (thm:root-fused-allocation of the paper) except the
ordered root anchors $\mathbf t$ and the root-fusion map $\phi$.  Put
\[
 \mathcal X_{\Gamma,\omega}(\mathbf t)
 :=\sum_{\phi\in\Phi_{\Gamma,\omega}(\mathbf t)}
 \mathcal A_{\Gamma,\omega}(\mathbf t,\phi).
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \sum_{\mathbf t\in\Delta_{q(\omega)}(m)}
 |\mathcal X_{\Gamma,\omega}(\mathbf t)|
 \le A_L^r(r+1)^B\mathfrak a_\Gamma D_\omega
 \prod_{\rho\in R(\omega)}(m\mathfrak e_\rho).}
\tag{3.4.1x$_9$}

Here $\mathfrak a_\Gamma$ retains the positive, already normalized
fixed-ribbon projective majorant and all unspent packet weights; the

used in (thm:root-fused-allocation of the paper).  Summing

$\log n$, short-gap scale, Bell factor, matching factorial, or component

 $\big(X_{in}^{(J)}\big)_{1\le i\le  k^{(J)}}$ be i.i.d. with

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-06T17:07:35.313136+00:00","domain":"set theory","id":"claim_c619e145faa54d71a70d2a407f2b55f1","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"The axiom of choice (AC) states: for every family (A_i)_{i in I} of nonempty sets, indexed by a set I, there exists a function c on I with c(i) in A_i for every i. Equivalently, every family of nonempty sets admits a choice function selecting one member of each set; every Cartesian product of nonempty sets is nonempty; every surjection has a right inverse; and every set of nonempty pairwise disjoint sets has a transversal selecting exactly one element from each. Over Zermelo-Fraenkel set theory ZF, AC is equivalent to Zorn's lemma, the well-ordering theorem, and Tychonoff's theorem for arbitrary compact spaces. AC asserts existence, not a specified construction; Zermelo formulated it in 1904 in order to prove the well-ordering theorem. AC is independent of ZF, assuming ZF is consistent: Godel (1938) established relative consistency of ZF+AC using the constructible universe, and Cohen (1963) established relative consistency of ZF+not-AC by forcing. Choice for every finite index set is a theorem of ZF. Choice for arbitrary countable families of nonempty sets is not provable in ZF in general.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T18:48:24.296313+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c663f0050fa00804b63b2073413d20b8a9c40d3970d812ab2b12faa032d9f2c2","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm optimali of arXiv:2605.10452, 'A secretary for Messrs. Luce and Mallows'] {\bf (P-2)}
Consider the secretary problem
with the  Mallows distribution with $q=q_n\in(0,1)$ in the case that the largest number is  of highest rank..

\noindent i. Let $q_n=1-\frac cn$, where $c>0$. Then the asymptotically optimal strategy is $\mathcal{S}^\uparrow(n,M_n^*)$, where
\begin{equation}
M_n^*\sim n\Big(\frac1c\log\big(1+\frac{e^c-1}e\big)\Big),
\end{equation}
 and the corresponding  limiting probability of success
is $\frac1e$:
$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}P_n^{\mathcal{M};q}(\mathcal{S}^\uparrow(n,M_n^*))=\frac1e.
$$
Also, $\lim_{c\to\infty} \frac1c\log\big(1+\frac{e^c-1}e\big)=1$ and $\lim_{c\to0} \frac1c\log\big(1+\frac{e^c-1}e\big)=\frac1e$.

\noindent ii.
Let $q_n=1-\frac c{n^\alpha}$, where $c>0$ and $\alpha\in(0,1)$. Then the asymptotically optimal strategy  is $\mathcal{S}^\uparrow(n,M_n^*)$, where
$$
n-M_n^*\sim\frac{n^\alpha}c,
$$
 and the corresponding limiting probability of success
is $\frac1e$:
$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}P_n^{\mathcal{M};q}(\mathcal{S}^\uparrow(n,M_n^*))=\frac1e.
$$
\noindent iii. Let $q\in(0,1)$.  Then the asymptotically optimal strategy  is $\mathcal{S}^\uparrow(n,M_n^*)$, where
$$
M_n^*=n-L, \ \text{where}\ L \ \text{satisfies}\ \frac q{1-q}\le L<\frac 1{1-q}.
$$
The corresponding limiting probability of success is given by
$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}P_n^{\mathcal{M};q}(\mathcal{S}^\uparrow(n,M_n^*))=(1-q)q^{L-1}L>\frac1e.
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:48:47.284240+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c66ceef19aa9d88a35c37ed0c3b56b4596efc977ac22d9acc6e886344d586d94","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defn def:smc of arXiv:2604.20629, 'Rates of forgetting for the sequentially Markov coalescent'] Let $(Y_{\ell})_{\ell\ge0}$ be a Markov
jump process on $(0,\infty)$ with the following dynamics. When $Y_{\ell}=y$,
the process waits an exponential time $r(y)=y$ before jumping,
at which time the process takes on
the new value $Y'=Uy+Z$, where $U\sim\mathrm{Unif}(0,1)$ is the
recombination time on the current tree expressed as a fraction of
the tree height, and $Z\sim\mathrm{Exp}(1)$ is the additional coalescence
time after the recombination event. 

Equivalently, one may construct $(Y_{\ell})$ from its embedded jump
chain and holding times as follows. Let $(X_{n})_{n\ge0}$ be the
jump chain and let $(E_{n})_{n\ge0}$ be i.i.d.\ $\mathrm{Exp}(1)$,
independent of the chain. Given $X_{n}$, define the holding time
\[
\Delta\ell_{n}:=\frac{E_{n}}{X_{n}}\ \sim\ \mathrm{Exp}(X_{n}),
\]
and jump locations $\ell_{0}:=0$, $\ell_{n+1}:=\ell_{n}+\Delta\ell_{n}$.
Then define 
\begin{align}
Y_{\ell} & :=X_{n}\quad\text{for }\ell\in[\ell_{n},\ell_{n+1}),\nonumber \\
X_{n+1} & :=U_{n}X_{n}+Z_{n},
\end{align}
where $(U_{n},Z_{n})$ are i.i.d.\ with $U_{n}\sim\mathrm{Unif}(0,1)$
and $Z_{n}\sim\mathrm{Exp}(1)$. In particular, $(Y_{\ell})$ is almost surely
piecewise constant.","status":"unverified"}

				-\frac{1}{2}N\xi''(q)\!\left(\int_q^1 \zeta([0,t])\,\mathrm{d} t\right)^{\!2}

{"assumptions":["The allocations are defined along sizes with positive conditioning probability.","0 < nu < lambda and the boundary-tilted law pi has generating-function radius one."],"created_at":"2026-10-10T06:51:51.362761+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c701f819aa156cb392336f5dc77d31cdfefe98e256ab50479dcc6ee2e7e58553","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[campaign result 2026-09-14, author_checked; reduction plus asserted conditional, not a solution] Svante Janson's Problem 18.39 in Simply generated trees, conditioned Galton-Watson trees, random allocations and condensation, Probability Surveys 9 (2012), arXiv:1112.0510, asks whether Y_(1)/n -> 0 in probability is possible in the condensation regime 0 < nu < lambda. Janson conjectures that it is not possible for the full sequence and, more strongly, that there are always epsilon > 0 and a subsequence along which Y_(1) >= epsilon n w.h.p. (Example 18.36 gives Y_(1)/n -> 0 in probability along a subsequence.) Setting: let w_k >= 0 with w_0 > 0, let Phi(z) = sum_k w_k z^k have radius rho in (0,infinity) with Phi(rho) < infinity, and put pi_k = w_k rho^k/Phi(rho), a law with generating-function radius one and finite mean nu > 0. Let m_n/n -> lambda > nu. (Y_1,...,Y_n) is n i.i.d. pi variables conditioned on sum m_n, Y_(1) = max_i Y_i, and M = (lambda-nu)n. Heuristic rate: carrying M in r = M/a boxes of size a has class weight binomial(n,r) pi_a^r up to the bulk's fluctuation, giving log P = M Lambda(a) + o(M) with Lambda(a) = [log pi_a + log(a/(lambda-nu)) + 1]/a. For pi_k ~ c k^(-beta) and for pi_a = exp(-a^gamma), 0<gamma<1, Lambda increases on large a, so the optimum is a = M (one box), matching the known condensation picture. Since limsup_a Lambda(a) = 0 and Lambda < 0 for large a, Lambda has infinitely many upper records a_1 < a_2 < ... (Lambda(a_j) > Lambda(a) for all a < a_j). The record asserts, as author-checked and with no proof given beyond reference to an analogous step for Problem 18.40 in a companion memo, the following Proposition: if for some epsilon > 0 and every C, along infinitely many records, Lambda(a_j) - max_{a <= epsilon a_j} Lambda(a) > C a_j^(-1/2), then along n_j = a_j/(lambda-nu), P(Y_(1) >= ((lambda-nu)/2) n_j) -> 1, so the conjecture holds. Caveat: the only derivation offered is the heuristic rate with an o(M) error, which is coarser than the order sqrt(a_j) resolution this hypothesis requires, so the record does not establish the Proposition. The record poses the open Question whether, for every law pi on Z_{>=0} with radius one and finite mean, [log pi_a + log a]/a has infinitely many records with gap exceeding a_j^(-1/2) below max_{a <= epsilon a_j} for some fixed epsilon > 0. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T22:31:02.822009+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c73143ec74e424ea68649a830e250439809c11442dd36f075e4edd190adabcb4","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary cor:finite-profile-transfer of arXiv:2609.01690, 'Iterated-sumset spectra: The complete exponent law and its rank geometry'] Fix $H\geq1$ and $k\geq2$, and let $G$ be a nontrivial torsion-free abelian
group.  The following four collections of truncated profiles are identical:
\[
 \bigl\{(|jA|)_{1\leq j\leq H}:A\subset G,\ |A|=k\bigr\},
 \quad
 \bigl\{(|jB|)_{1\leq j\leq H}:B\subset\mathbb Z,\ |B|=k\bigr\},
\]
\[
 \bigl\{(|P^{\times j}|)_{1\leq j\leq H}:
       P\subset\mathbb Z_{>0},\ |P|=k\bigr\},
 \quad
 \bigl\{(H_{C_B}(j))_{1\leq j\leq H}:
       B\subset\mathbb Z,\ |B|=k\bigr\},
\]
where $P^{\times j}$ is the $j$-fold product set and $C_B$ is the projective
monomial curve attached to $B$ over an arbitrary field.  More strongly,
equip the subgroup generated by an additive realization with a
translation-invariant linear order.  Its complete equality-and-order table
through degree $H$ then has an integer exponent representative.  The
resulting sumset, product-set, and monomial-curve exponent models have
identical ordered tables, active ranks, and relation-birth degrees through
$H$.

$B=\{0=b_0<\cdots<b_{k-1}\}$ with
\begin{equation}
 b_{k-1}\leq dH^{d-1}\prod_{i=1}^r p_i
 \leq(k-1-r)H^{k-2},
 \qquad d=k-1-r,
\end{equation}
where $r$ and $p_i$ are its active rank and birth degrees through $H$.
The universal exponent $k-2$ for preserving the complete truncated table is
best possible.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-28T02:39:12.425148+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c7c9d84c15d51e3f2b3f5f8d8c898c0968444eb9dadf9f8776f20251333d57b5","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Dfn of arXiv:2412.08236, 'Aging and sub-aging for Bouchaud trap models on resistance metric spaces'] [{The product functor}]
  Fix $N \in \mathbb{N}$.
  Let $(\tau^{(k)})_{k=1}^{N}$ be 
  a sequence of functors.
  The \textit{product functor} $\tau = \prod_{k=1}^{N} \tau^{(k)}$ is defined as follows:
  \begin{enumerate}
    \item
      For every $(S, d^{S}, \rho_{S}) \in \mathfrak{M}$, 
      we set $\tau(S) \coloneqq \prod_{k=1}^{N} \tau^{(k)}(S)$.
      We equip $\tau(S)$ with the max product metric (cf.\ (equation 2. eq: max product metric of the paper)).
    \item 
      For every $(S_{i}, d^{S_{i}}, \rho_{S_{i}}),\, i=1,2$ 
      and root-and-distance-preserving map $f: S_{1} \to S_{2}$, 
      we set $\tau_{f} \coloneqq \prod_{k=1}^{N} \tau_{f}^{(k)}$, that is, 
      $\tau_{f}: \tau(S_{1}) \to \tau(S_{2})$ is a distance-preserving map given by 
      \begin{equation}
        \tau_{f}\bigl( (a_{k})_{k=1}^{N} \bigr) \coloneqq \bigl( \tau^{(k)}_{f}(a_{k}) \bigr)_{k=1}^{N}.
      \end{equation}
  \end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["(a): f integrable on R","(b): the periodization converges everywhere to a continuous function AND the Fourier transform is absolutely summable over the integers","(c): f continuous with (1+|x|)^{-1-delta} decay of both f and its transform","integrability alone does NOT give the pointwise identity"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:49:39.263262+00:00","domain":"harmonic analysis on Euclidean space","id":"claim_c871045185872c50e3ad107b05bbe60ce99326ffffae1aec8481b784ad7e885a","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Convention $\\hat f(\\xi)=\\int_{\\mathbb R}f(x)e^{-2\\pi i x\\xi}dx$. (a) (Always, as an $L^1$ identity) If $f\\in L^1(\\mathbb R)$, the periodization $Pf(x)=\\sum_{n\\in\\mathbb Z}f(x+n)$ converges absolutely for a.e. $x$, $Pf\\in L^1(\\mathbb T)$ with $\\|Pf\\|_{L^1(\\mathbb T)}\\le\\|f\\|_1$, and $\\widehat{Pf}(k)=\\hat f(k)$ for all $k\\in\\mathbb Z$. (b) (Pointwise identity) If in addition $\\sum_nf(x+n)$ converges for every $x$ to a continuous function and $\\sum_k|\\hat f(k)|<\\infty$, then $\\sum_{n\\in\\mathbb Z}f(x+n)=\\sum_{k\\in\\mathbb Z}\\hat f(k)e^{2\\pi i kx}$ for every $x$; taking $x=0$, $\\sum_nf(n)=\\sum_k\\hat f(k)$. (c) (Convenient sufficient condition) If $f$ is continuous and there are $C,\\delta>0$ with $|f(x)|\\le C(1+|x|)^{-1-\\delta}$ and $|\\hat f(\\xi)|\\le C(1+|\\xi|)^{-1-\\delta}$, then (b) applies and both series converge absolutely; this holds for every $f\\in\\mathcal S(\\mathbb R)$. (d) Scaled and multidimensional forms: for $T>0$, $\\sum_nf(nT)=T^{-1}\\sum_k\\hat f(k/T)$; for $f\\in\\mathcal S(\\mathbb R^d)$ and the lattice $\\mathbb Z^d$, $\\sum_{n\\in\\mathbb Z^d}f(x+n)=\\sum_{k\\in\\mathbb Z^d}\\hat f(k)e^{2\\pi i k\\cdot x}$; more generally for a full-rank lattice $\\Lambda$ with dual $\\Lambda^*$ and covolume $|\\Lambda|$, $\\sum_{\\lambda\\in\\Lambda}f(\\lambda)=|\\Lambda|^{-1}\\sum_{\\mu\\in\\Lambda^*}\\hat f(\\mu)$. Classic application (Jacobi theta transformation): $\\sum_ne^{-\\pi n^2t}=t^{-1/2}\\sum_ne^{-\\pi n^2/t}$ for $t>0$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T12:13:31.904720+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c87a764610fbe61ef1c23644c0f9f4938a21a1f9ccdb4efc4a33ff94d96de279","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:generalcoupling of arXiv:2506.10765, 'A General Coupling for Ising Models and Beyond'] Let $\Omega$ and $\Sigma$ be two finite sets, $\rho$ and $\gamma$ be probability measures on $\Omega$ and $\Sigma$ respectively, and $f: \Omega \to 2^{\Sigma}$ be a function\footnote{Here, $2^{\Sigma}$ is the power set of $\Sigma$.}. For each $\eta \in \Sigma$, let
    $f^{-1}(\eta):=\{\omega \in \Omega \mid \eta \in f(\omega)\}.$
     Suppose that $ \sum_{\omega \in \Omega, \eta \in \Sigma} \rho[\omega] \gamma[\eta] 1\! \!1[\eta \in f(\omega)] > 0$ and then define a coupling probability measure on $\Omega\times\Sigma$ by
	\[\mathscr{P}[\omega,\eta]\propto \rho[\omega] \gamma[\eta] 1\! \!1[\eta \in f(\omega)],~\forall (\omega, \eta)\in\Omega\times\Sigma. \] 

	\begin{enumerate}
    \item[(a)] The marginal of $\mathscr{P}$ on $\Omega$, denoted by  $\mathscr{P}_{\Omega}$, satisfies $ \mathscr{P}_{\Omega}[\omega]  \propto \gamma[f(\omega)]\rho[\omega]$ for each $\omega \in \Omega$. 
		\item[(b)] The marginal of $\mathscr{P}$ on $\Sigma$, denoted by $\mathscr{P}_{\Sigma}$, satisfies $ \mathscr{P}_{\Sigma}[\eta] \propto  \rho[f^{-1}(\eta)] \gamma[\eta] $ for each $\eta \in \Sigma$.   

\item[(c)] For each $\omega\in\Omega$ with $\mathscr{P}_{\Omega}[\omega]\neq 0$,  the conditional measure $\mathscr{P}[\cdot | \omega]$ on $\Sigma$ is $\gamma[\cdot \mid f(\omega)]$.
        \item[(d)]   For each $\eta\in\Sigma$ with $\mathscr{P}_{\Sigma}[\eta]\neq 0$, the conditional measure $\mathscr{P}[\cdot|\eta] $ on $\Omega$ is $\rho[\cdot \mid f^{-1}(\eta)]$.
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:38.543907+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c894786f1b55507dfb078a06491f9f69fe1f01bd76b485d4469c8716a85154c8","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"For a real parameter delta >= 0 the SQUARED BESSEL PROCESS of dimension delta started at y >= 0, written BESQ^delta, is the unique strong solution of dY_t = 2 sqrt( |Y_t| ) dW_t + delta dt with Y_0 = y; the solution is nonnegative, and pathwise uniqueness holds despite the non-Lipschitz diffusion coefficient by the Yamada-Watanabe criterion, which requires only Holder continuity of exponent 1/2. The BESSEL PROCESS of dimension delta, BES^delta, is X_t = sqrt(Y_t); for X > 0 it solves dX_t = dW_t + ((delta - 1)/(2 X_t)) dt. When delta = d is a positive INTEGER, BES^d started at |x| has the law of the radial part |B_t| of a d-dimensional Brownian motion started at x - a fact that makes the family the natural interpolation of radial Brownian motion to non-integer dimension. ADDITIVITY: BESQ^delta started at y and an independent BESQ^{delta'} started at y' add to a BESQ^{delta + delta'} started at y + y'; this holds for the SQUARED process and is false for the Bessel process itself. The index nu = delta/2 - 1 is the other common parameterisation and is the one that appears in the modified Bessel functions of the transition density; delta and nu must not be confused. For delta < 2 the boundary point 0 is reached and a boundary convention (absorbing or instantaneously reflecting) must be specified; for delta >= 2 the point 0 is never reached from y > 0 and no convention is needed. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T10:55:57.000374+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c8b91c6ad846745543ab01427ecc658f4873f7929768971f718375e64637a53a","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 1 (Main theorem) of arXiv:2609.02788, '\textbf{Quantized Einstein Metrics on \(S^7\) with \(SU(3)\)-Symmetry}'] For the standard cohomogeneity-one adjoint action of \(SU(3)\) on \(S^7\),
there exist infinitely many pairwise non-isometric smooth invariant Einstein
metrics.  They may be normalized by
\[
 \Ric(g_n)=6g_n,
\]
and have principal orbit \(SU(3)/T^2\) and two singular orbits
\(\mathbb{CP}^2\).

More precisely, the metrics can be chosen so that, if \(b_n\) denotes the
scale of the initial singular orbit and \(\beta_n\) its anisotropy parameter,
then
\[
 b_n\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 \beta_n\longrightarrow c_*<0,
\]
where \(c_*\) is the Ricci-flat threshold of
Proposition~\ref{prop:threshold}.  Moreover, the sequence may be indexed so that, for some phase constant
\(\theta_*\in\mathbb R/\pi\mathbb Z\),
\[
 \frac{\sqrt{15}}2\log\frac1{b_n}
 =n\pi+\theta_*+o(1),
\]
and consequently
\[
 \frac{b_{n+1}}{b_n}\longrightarrow e^{-2\pi/\sqrt{15}}.
\]
Let \(h_2\) denote the nonnormal Einstein metric on \(SU(3)/T^2\)
whose Ricci-flat cone is
\[
 dr^2+r^2h_2,
 \qquad
 f_1=f_2=\frac r{\sqrt5},\quad
 f_3=\sqrt{\frac25}\,r,
\]
and let \(g_{\RF,*}\) be the complete Ricci-flat threshold metric of
Proposition~\ref{prop:threshold}.  If \(p_n^\pm\) are points on the two
singular orbits, then
\[
 (S^7,b_n^{-2}g_n,p_n^\pm)
 \longrightarrow (M_*,g_{\RF,*},p_*)
\]
in pointed smooth Cheeger--Gromov sense.  On the complementary scale,
\[
 g_n\longrightarrow dt^2+\sin^2t\,h_2
\]
smoothly locally on \((0,\pi)\times SU(3)/T^2\).  Finally, there are
constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that
\[
 c b_n^{-2}\le \sup_{S^7}|\Rm(g_n)|\le C b_n^{-2}.
\]
Let \(K_{02}^{(n)}\) denotes the sectional curvature of \(g_n\) in the
two-plane spanned by the radial direction and a unit vector tangent to
the third isotropy summand. At eithe singular orbit,
$$
 b_n^2K_{02}^{(n)}\longrightarrow-\frac{1+2c_*^2}{2}.
$$
Consequently,
$$
 \frac{|K_{02}^{(n+1)}|}{|K_{02}^{(n)}|}
 \longrightarrow e^{4\pi/\sqrt{15}}.
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:26:47.164177+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c8dd5d6dbd908dc76ffcd01c3c853b2848ddab7bef6bfcc98f9f6c9096bc819d","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem 32 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] If case \eqref{i:fp-case1} of Remark~\ref{r:fp.cases} does not hold, then in any local
   maximizer $(\vvvv,\xxxx,\vwww)$ of the function $F_\diamond$ defined by \eqref{e:fp-Fdiam}, the vector $\vwww$ must be entrywise positive.
\begin{proof}
    If case \eqref{i:fp-case1} does not hold, we have $\hv_1 > 0$, $\hx > 0$, or $\mu_1 < \alpha$. We assume for contradiction that $\vwww$ is not entrywise positive, and divide the analysis into a few cases:
\begin{itemize}
\item     \emph{Case 1:} $\hv_1 > 0$ or $\hx > 0$. In this case, let  $\www_{j_1}$ be a positive entry of $\vwww$, which must exist due to the constraint $(\mu,\vwww) = 1$. Now suppose for contradiction that we have $\www_{j_2} = 0$. For small positive $\delta$, the replacement
\[(\www_{j_1},\www_{j_2})
\mapsto \bigg(\www_{j_1} - \frac{\mu_{j_2}}{\mu_{j_1}} \delta, \delta
    \bigg)\]
increases the value of the budget
    \[\frac1\alpha
    \bigg( \sum_{j=1}^s \mu_j (\www_j)^{1/2}\bigg)^2\]
by $\Theta(\delta^{1/2})$. It follows that we may replace $\vvv_1$ with $\vvv_1 + \Theta(\delta^{1/2})$, or $\xxxx$ with $\xxxx + \Theta(\delta^{1/2})$, while remaining inside the set $S_\diamond(\lambda,\mu)$. Recalling
\eqref{e:fp-Fdiam}, we can do this in a way which increases the value of $F_\diamond$ by $\Theta(\delta^{1/2})$, contradicting the assumption that we were at a local maximizer.

\item \emph{Case 2:} $\hv_1 < 0$, $\hx \le 0$, and $\mu_1 < \alpha$.
We divide further into two cases:
\begin{itemize}
\item     \emph{Case 2a:} $\vvvv$ is not identically zero.
    As above, let $\www_{j_1} > 0$ and $\www_{j_2} = 0$.
    Further let $\vvv_{j_3} > 0$, and note that $\hv_{j_3} \le \hv_1 < 0$.
    Therefore the replacement
    \[
        (\www_{j_1},\www_{j_2},\vvv_{j_3}) \mapsto
        \lt(\www_{j_1} - \frac{\mu_{j_2}}{\mu_{j_1}} \delta, \delta,
        \vvv_{j_3} - \Theta(\delta^{1/2})\rt)
    \]
    improves \eqref{e:fp-Fdiam} by $\Theta(\delta^{1/2})$ while remaining inside $S_\diamond(\lambda,\mu)$.
    This gives a contradiction.

\item     \emph{Case 2b:} $\vvvv$ is identically zero. Then the constraints defining $S_\diamond(\lambda,\mu)$ reduce to
 \beq
        
        1 + \xxxx \le \frac1\alpha \bigg(\sum_{j=1}^s \mu_j (\www_j)^{1/2}\bigg)^2\,, \quad
        (\mu,\vwww) = 1\,.\eeq
    Since $\mu_1 < \alpha$, we have $\vwww \neq (1/\mu_1, 0, \ldots, 0)$.
   Thus there must exist at least one index $j_1\ge2$ for which $\www_{j_1}$ is positive.
    If $\www_1 = 0$, then the replacement
    \[(\www_1,\www_{j_1}) \mapsto
        \bigg(\delta,\www_{j_1} - \frac{\mu_1}{\mu_{j_1}} \delta\bigg)\] improves the value of \eqref{e:fp-Fdiam}
while remaining inside $S_\diamond$.
    Therefore we must have $\www_1 > 0$.
    Finally, if $\www_{j_2} = 0$ for any $j_2 \ge 2$, the replacement
    \[
        (\www_1,\www_{j_1},\www_{j_2}) \rightarrow
        \lt(\www_1 + \delta^{2/3}, \www_{j_1} - \frac{\mu_1}{\mu_{j_1}} \delta^{2/3} - \frac{\mu_{j_2}}{\mu_{j_1}} \delta, \delta \rt)
    \]
    improves the value of \eqref{e:fp-Fdiam} by $\Theta(\delta^{2/3})$ while remaining inside $S_\diamond$.
\end{itemize}
\end{itemize}
This concludes the proof.
\end{proof}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-08-09T16:48:21.513714+00:00","domain":"functional analysis","id":"claim_c8df104912a240938197f2669f3805c8","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let H be an inner product space with norm ||x|| = sqrt(<x,x>). If H is real, the inner product is recovered from the norm by <x,y> = (||x+y||^2 - ||x-y||^2) / 4 for all x, y in H. If H is complex, <x,y> = (1/4) sum_{k=0}^3 i^k ||x + i^k y||^2, equivalently <x,y> = (1/4)[(||x+y||^2 - ||x-y||^2) + i(||x+iy||^2 - ||x-iy||^2)]. Combined with the parallelogram-law characterization, this shows a norm comes from an inner product exactly when it satisfies the parallelogram law, and in that case the identity above is the only possible inner product inducing it.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T17:03:59.374369+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c8e8d5862c639944cb0487f49591d4f0ca638d936f88c94d80bb799ba8187029","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:exist of arXiv:2507.08757, 'Strong existence and uniqueness of the tilt-indexed Busemann process in the planar corner '] {\rm[Jan-Ras-20-aop]} There exists a probability space $(\widehat\Omega,\widehat{\mathfrak{S}},\widehat\mathbb{P})$,  equipped with an additive group of continuous bijections $\widehat{T}=\{\widehat{T}_x:x\in\mathbb{Z}^2\}$ and satisfying the hypotheses of Section (sec:probsp of the paper), on which there exists a stochastic process
\begin{align}    
    \bigl({\widehat B}^{h{\scaleobj{0.9}{\boxempty}}}(x,y) : x,y\in\mathbb{Z}^2, h \in -\partial \textup{g}(\mathcal U),\, {\scaleobj{0.9}{\boxempty}} \in \{+,-\}\bigr)
\end{align}
with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}  [label={\rm(\alph*)}, ref={\rm\alph*}]   \itemsep=3pt
\item \textup{(}No $\pm$ distinction at fixed $h$\textup{)} For each $h \in -\partial \textup{g}(\mathcal U)$, 
\[
\widehat\mathbb{P}\bigl\{{\widehat B}^{h-}(x,y) = {\widehat B}^{h+}(x,y)\bigr\}=1.
\]
When ${\widehat B}^{h-}({\widehat\omega},x,y) = {\widehat B}^{h+}({\widehat\omega},x,y)$, call the common value ${\widehat B}^h({\widehat\omega}, x,y)$.
\item \textup{(}Generalized Busemann function\textup{)} For each $h \in -\partial \textup{g}(\mathcal U), {\widehat B}^h \in \widehat{\mathcal{K}}$.  

\item \textup{(}Mean $-h$\textup{)} For each $h \in -\partial \textup{g}(\mathcal U),$ $\widehat\mathbb{E}[{\widehat B}^h(0,e_i)] = -h \cdot e_i.$
\item \textup{(}Monotonicity\textup{)} For $h,h'\in -\partial \textup{g}(\mathcal U)$ with $h \cdot e_1 \leq h' \cdot e_1$, all $x \in \mathbb{Z}^2$, and $\widehat\mathbb{P}$-almost every ${\widehat\omega}$
\[ 
    {\widehat B}^{h-}(x,x+e_1) \geq  {\widehat B}^{h+}(x,x+e_1) \geq  {\widehat B}^{h'-}(x,x+e_1) \geq  {\widehat B}^{h'-}(x,x+e_1)  
\]
and
\[ 
    {\widehat B}^{h-}(x,x+e_2) \leq  {\widehat B}^{h+}(x,x+e_2) \leq  {\widehat B}^{h'-}(x,x+e_2) \leq  {\widehat B}^{h'-}(x,x+e_2).
\]
\item \textup{(}Left-/right-continuity\textup{)} For $\widehat\mathbb{P}$ almost all ${\widehat\omega}$, for all $h\in -\partial \textup{g}(\mathcal U)$,
\begin{equation*}\begin{aligned}
{\widehat B}^{h-}(x,y) = \lim_{\substack{-\partial \textup{g} (\mathcal U)\hspace{0.5pt}\ni\hspace{0.5pt}  h' \to h\\ h'\cdot e_1 \nearrow h \cdot e_1}} {\widehat B}^{h\pm}(x,y) \qquad \text{ and } {\widehat B}^{h-}(x,y) = \lim_{\substack{-\partial \textup{g} (\mathcal U)\hspace{0.5pt}\ni\hspace{0.5pt}  h' \to h\\ h'\cdot e_1 \searrow h \cdot e_1}} {\widehat B}^{h\pm}(x,y).
\end{aligned}\end{equation*}
\item \textup{(}Backward independence\textup{)} For any $I \subset \mathbb{Z}^2$, the random variables $\{\omega_x, {\widehat B}^{h\pm}(x,y) : y \geq x,\, x \in I,\, h \in -\partial \textup{g}(\mathcal U)\}$ are independent of the  weights  $\{\omega_x : \forall z\in I , \, x  \not\geq z \}$ behind $I$.\qedhere
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}
